title: Land a tuned spec version: the dispatch names {id, version}, and the runner runs the version it names

story.i_want_to: a merged spec_tuner draft (a template at version 2 or later) to be the version the next dispatch of that kind actually runs
story.so_that: the improvement loop US-48.13 built closes; today a proposed draft can be scored and merged but never runs, because the runner picks version 1 of every kind

rationale: Found while documenting Epic 48 (US-48.14). The runner resolves a dispatch's template with Templates.for_dispatch/1, which keys on kind alone and holds only version-1 templates (@by_kind in lib/loopctl_runner/templates.ex). The runner contract's dispatch payload carries no spec field; only agent_result names {id, version}. So no code path exists for running a version-2 template, and every tuning draft with to_version > 1 is unreachable.

acceptance_criteria.description: loopctl's registry names one LIVE version per spec id, and every dispatch payload loopctl sends carries spec {id, version} for that live version; the runner contract is bumped (minor) and the vendored copy in loopctl-runner stays byte-identical.

The runner resolves a dispatch by the {id, version} it names (Templates.fetch/1). A dispatch naming a version this runner does not hold is refused with a stable code and is never run on a different version.

A runner on the earlier contract, which sends no spec field, keeps getting dispatches only for version-1 specs; loopctl never sends a version > 1 to a runner whose declared templates do not include it.
agent_result's spec must equal the dispatch's spec; a mismatch is refused, so an outcome row can never be credited to a version that did not run.
Raising a spec's live version is a merged change to the registry, never an API call, so the spec_tuner (which writes no template and opens no PR) still cannot promote its own draft.

test_cases.name: the named version runs
steps: registry lists triage live at version 2; runner declares triage@1 and triage@2

test_cases.name: a runner without the version is not sent it
steps: runner declares only triage@1; live version is 2
expected_results: no triage dispatch is placed on that runner

test_cases.name: mismatched result spec is refused
steps: dispatch named triage@2; agent_result names triage@1

test_cases.name: tenant isolation
steps: two tenants, each with a triage dispatch
expected_results: each tenant's ledger and outcome rows carry only its own dispatch's spec

technical_notes: Spans loopctl (registry live version, payload, contract) and loopctl-runner (Templates.for_dispatch/1 keyed on spec, declared templates).
The runner's join already declares {id, version} pairs (Templates.specs/1, contract 1.25.0), so loopctl's capability matching can key on them.
